scope: the entity block starts at BIT 1307, and both gate bits (1307, 1308) read as 1 in our body - yet the count is still 0, so the count path is gated by something else
what_1307_means: the bit reader keeps [+0x20] as an absolute bit position, so the entity block begins at bit 1307
gate bit 1 is therefore bit 1307 and gate bit 2 is bit 1308
bit 1307 is the LAST bit of the 1308-bit hybrid header, and that header is all ones at the end (bits 1300..1307)
bit 1308 is the first bit of our playerState block, which we set to 1 (has-ps)
so BOTH gate bits should read 1 in our body
the_puzzle: if both gates read 1, the code falls through to the count reader 0x66ED70
and 0x66ED70 reads the byte at the BYTE cursor [+0x1C] = 164, i.e. body[164]
in runs/snapshot-ent1.bin body[164] was set to 0x01 - and the count STILL read 0
so either the gates did not both read 1, or 0x66ED70 is reading from a different base than the body start
the_two_consistent_explanations: (a) the gate at 0x671678/0x671685 is not the first read of the block: 0x471DA3 calls 0x671650, and something before that consumes bits, so the effective gate indices are higher than 1307/1308

(b) 0x66ED70 reads at [stream+0x1C] but that field is an index into a buffer whose base is [stream+8] or [stream+0xC], not the body start - the disassembly shows two different buffers selected by comparing against [stream+0x14]
next: read the two buffers in 0x66ED70: [edx+8] and [edx+0xC] are two separate pointers, and the read picks one depending on whether the cursor is below or above the window start
probing both pointers at 0x671650 tells us which buffer body[164] actually lives in
